title: Why Doesn't Your Stomach Digest Itself?
description:
Why doesn't stomach acid digest your own stomach? Your stomach acid can drop to pH 1.5, but a mucus layer full of bicarbonate, switched-off pepsin and a lining that rebuilds itself every few days keep it from eating you.

Sources:
https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/why-the-stomach-does-not-digest-its/
https://www.gi.alaska.edu/alaska-science-forum/why-doesnt-stomach-digest-itself
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastric_acid

Animated in the Flat-Vector Science style.

topic: Why doesn't your stomach digest itself?
script:
Your stomach acid dissolves metal,
so how does your stomach survive it,
three times a day?
The acid can drop to pH one point five.
Strong enough to eat through zinc,
and turn a steak to mush.
But your stomach has three tricks.
Trick one: a thick blanket of mucus,
loaded with bicarbonate,
basically baking soda.
So right against the wall,
the acid gets neutralized.
Trick two: pepsin, the meat-eating enzyme,
is made switched off.
It only turns on out in the acid,
away from your cells.
Trick three: your lining sheds around half a million cells,
every minute,
and rebuilds itself every few days.
So damage gets replaced before it spreads.
Your stomach isn't acid-proof.
It just heals faster than it melts.
Which trick would you want: the slime, the switch, or the shedding?
key_facts: Stomach acid can reach about pH 1.5 (normal range roughly 1.5-3.5)
A mucus layer rich in bicarbonate neutralizes acid right at the stomach wall
Pepsin is secreted as inactive pepsinogen and is activated by acid in the stomach cavity
The lining sheds roughly 500,000 cells a minute and renews itself every few days (about 3-5 days)
